1.title: Monitoring with Azure Monitor
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen: Monitoring with Azure Monitor. It covers the exam area Monitor and maintain Azure resources. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Interpret metrics in Azure Monitor. Configure log settings in Azure Monitor. Query and analyze logs in Azure Monitor. Set up alert rules, action groups and alert processing rules. Configure and interpret monitoring of virtual machines, storage accounts and networks by using Azure Monitor Insights. Use Azure Network Watcher and Connection Monitor. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Monitor and maintain Azure resources (ten-fifteen percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: Azure Monitor at a glance
1.text: Azure Monitor at a glance. Azure Monitor collects, analyzes and acts on telemetry from Azure and other environments.

1.title: Azure Monitor at a glance, continued
1.text: Azure Monitor at a glance. The figure shows this: Azure Monitor: data sources feed metrics and logs, which drive insights, alerts and actions.

1.title: Azure Monitor at a glance, continued
1.text: Azure Monitor at a glance. Metrics. What it is: Numeric time series (C P U %, bytes in). Stored: Azure Monitor metrics database, near real time, kept ninety-three days. Logs. What it is: Records and events with fields. Stored: Log Analytics workspace, queried with K Q L. Activity log. What it is: Subscription-level control-plane events (who created, changed or deleted what). Stored: Kept ninety days; send it to a workspace for longer.

1.title: Metrics
1.text: Metrics. Metrics Explorer charts metrics, lets you split by dimension (for example per instance), apply aggregation (average, max, count) and pin to dashboards. Platform metrics are collected automatically; guest O S metrics need an agent.

1.title: Logs and diagnostic settings
1.text: Logs and diagnostic settings. Resource logs are not collected by default. A diagnostic setting on a resource sends platform logs and metrics to a destination. Log Analytics workspace. Query and alert with K Q L. Storage account. Cheap long-term archive. Event Hub. Stream to external tools. A Log Analytics workspace is queried in Logs with Kusto Query Language, for example. Azure Activity where Operation Name Value contains delete project Time Generated, Caller, Resource Group. Exam tip: "Resource logs are missing" equals create a diagnostic setting. "Query across logs with a language" equals Log Analytics and K Q L.

1.title: Alerts
1.text: Alerts. Alert rule. Scope (resources) plus condition (metric threshold, log query result, activity log event) plus action group. Alert types. Metric, log search, activity log. Action group. What happens: email, S M S, push, voice, webhook, Logic App, Azure Function, runbook. Alert processing rule. Modify alerts after they fire: suppress notifications (for example during maintenance windows) or add action groups. Severity. zero (critical) to four (verbose).

1.title: Alerts, continued
1.text: Alerts. The figure shows this: An alert rule with scope, condition and action group, plus a processing rule for maintenance. Exam tip: "Stop alert emails during planned maintenance without deleting the rules" equals an alert processing rule that suppresses notifications.

1.title: Insights and Network Watcher
1.text: Insights and Network Watcher. V M insights. Performance and dependency map of V Ms (needs the Azure Monitor Agent). Storage insights. Capacity, latency, availability across storage accounts. Network insights. Topology and health of network resources. Network Watcher. I P flow verify, next hop, connection troubleshoot, packet capture, N S G flow logs, topology. Connection Monitor. Continuously tests connectivity and latency between endpoints and alerts on failures. Exam tip: Resource logs are not collected until you create a diagnostic setting. Metrics are collected automatically.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. An administrator needs to know who deleted a virtual machine. Where should they look? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The Activity log. The Activity log records control-plane operations such as deletions.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A storage account's resource logs must be queried with K Q L. What must be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A diagnostic setting sending logs to a Log Analytics workspace. Diagnostic settings route resource logs to a destination.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An alert must email the on-call team when C P U exceeds eighty percent. What should be created? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A metric alert rule with an action group. Metric alert rules trigger action groups.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Notifications must be suppressed during a maintenance window without deleting alert rules. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: An alert processing rule. Processing rules can suppress notifications on a schedule.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which tool continuously tests connectivity and latency between two endpoints? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Connection Monitor. Connection Monitor performs ongoing connectivity tests.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. How long does the Activity log keep events by default? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: ninety days. The Activity log is retained for ninety days.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What language queries Log Analytics? Answer: Kusto Query Language. Question two. How long are platform metrics kept? Answer: ninety-three days. Question three. What does an action group define? Answer: What happens when an alert fires (notifications and actions).

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name two diagnostic setting destinations. Answer: For example a Log Analytics workspace and a storage account. Question five. Name three alert rule types. Answer: Metric, log search and activity log. Question six. Which feature gives a dependency map of V Ms? Answer: V M insights.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Data: metrics (ninety-three days), logs (workspace, K Q L), Activity log (ninety days). Diagnostic settings: send resource logs to workspace, storage, Event Hub. Alerts: rule equals scope plus condition plus action group; processing rules suppress or add actions. Insights: V M, Storage, Network; Network Watcher; Connection Monitor.
